key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent optimization of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial assignments.
engineering_relevance: The framework designs highly porous scaffolds that closely match target bone mechanics while enforcing mechanical and feature-size constraints.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells with a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometries and spatial assignments under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: Eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% error across six target moduli; human femoral designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance constraints satisfied within 2%, and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks; fabrication accuracy, fatigue performance, and biological integration still require experimental validation.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
